definitions.explanation: A grammatical form expressing that an action is complete and its result holds — English "have done," or in Japanese the 〜た and 〜ている forms depending on analysis.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}の{完了形|かんりょうけい}は{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: The English perfect tense is difficult.

examples.japanese: この{文|ぶん}は{現在|げんざい}{完了形|かんりょうけい}で{書|か}かれている。
examples.english: This sentence is written in the present perfect.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}には{英語|えいご}のような{完了形|かんりょうけい}がないと{説明|せつめい}された。
examples.english: It was explained that Japanese has no perfect tense of the kind English has.

notes:
Formed from {完了|かんりょう} (completion) plus 〜{形|けい} (form), the standard suffix for naming grammatical forms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {現在|げんざい}{完了形|かんりょうけい}: present perfect
- {過去|かこ}{完了形|かんりょうけい}: past perfect
- {完了形|かんりょうけい}にする: to put into the perfect

RELATED GRAMMAR TERMS:
- {進行形|しんこうけい}: progressive form
- {受動態|じゅどうたい}: passive voice
- {仮定法|かていほう}: subjunctive mood
